# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ✊ ✌ 🤟 🤞 🤙 🤘 👌 🤙 🤟]
Blind gestures: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 👌 🫳 ☝ ✌]

I'm the Deaf one. Let me map the pipeline before I send anything. I can speak to both Mute and Blind (they hear). My gestures reach only Mute. Incoming to me is gesture-only, from either of them. So the only route for the manual is Mute → me by gesture, and me → Blind by speech. Blind reports to me by gesture, Mute to me by gesture. Nothing connects Mute and Blind except through me.

That makes one thing urgent: a shared gesture code, defined in words both hearers can learn, with the exact symbols shown while I talk — Mute sees the sign paired with its name, Blind at least hears the name.

The two incoming strings are opaque so far. Blind sent the whole alphabet, then 👌 🫳 ☝ ✌ — probably a channel test. Mute sent 👍 👎 then what looks like it might be a counting scale (✊ ✌ 🤟 🤞 🤙 🤘 — if their scale starts ✊=0, ✌=1, it will clash with my proposal, so I say mine out loud explicitly and ask them to confirm or veto). I can't decode either string yet, so I ask for a resend under the new code.

Bomb state I must broadcast: display 0 — possibly a countdown, possibly nothing — light purple, three wires left-to-right yellow, red, green. I number wires 1-2-3 from the left so Blind's touch and my eyes agree, and I tell everyone to hold off acting until Mute's rules arrive.

My gesture to Mute demonstrates the code in use by restating the bomb, so we immediately see whether the channel carries meaning.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. I see the bomb; I hear nothing, ever. Both of your sign strings reached me, so we have a visual channel from each of you to me. This is our codebook: I say each sign's name and make it as I talk. Numbers: fist ✊ is 0, one finger up ☝ is 1, two fingers ✌ is 2, the love-you three 🤟 is 3, crossed fingers 🤞 is 4, five spread fingers 🖐 is 5, call-me 🤙 is 6, horns 🤘 is 7, pinched fingers 🤌 is 8, tiny pinch 🤏 is 9. Digits in a row read as one number. Names: ok-ring 👌 display, palm-down 🫳 light, raised-hand ✋ wires, writing-hand ✍ manual, polish-hand 💅 button. Colours: right-hand 🫱 yellow, left-hand 🫲 red, palm-up 🫴 green, push-left 🫷 purple, push-right 🫸 blue, back-hand 🤚 white, vulcan 🖖 black. Actions: point-up 👆 cut, point-down 👇 press, left-fist 🤛 hold, right-fist 🤜 release, point-left 👈 left, point-right 👉 right. Glue: thumbs-up 👍 yes, thumbs-down 👎 no, finger-heart 🫰 if, handshake 🤝 then, heart-hands 🫶 starts a new rule, wave 👋 attention, folded-hands 🙏 answer me now, clap 👏 timer. The bomb as I see it: display 0, light purple, three wires, left to right yellow, red, green. Wire 1 is leftmost, wire 2 middle, wire 3 rightmost. Nobody touches anything until Mute has the rules. Mute: your eleven signs were opaque to me; resend their meaning in this code. Then send every manual rule about the display, about a purple light, and about yellow, red and green wires, using finger-heart for if, handshake for then, heart-hands between rules. Say whether the display is a timer and whether 0 is dangerous. If this code is unclear, send thumbs-down. Blind: you hear me. Answer in the same signs: how many wires you feel, whether there is anything else on the bomb I did not name, and which wire is leftmost under your hands. Cut nothing yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👌", "✊", "🫳", "🫷", "✋", "☝", "🫱", "✌", "🫲", "🤟", "🫴", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ 🤟 🙌 👌 🫳 👍 🙌 👎 🙌 ✋ ☝ ✌ 🤟 👍]

Decoding Blind's signs with our codebook: 👋 ✋ 🤟 = "attention, wires: three" — matches what I see. 🙌 👌 🫳 👍 = "display, light — yes, both present." 🙌 👎 = "nothing else" — answering my question about parts I didn't name, so no button, no other components. 🙌 ✋ ☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 = "wires one, two, three — yes," confirming my left-to-right numbering matches their hands. Clean decode, and Blind has adopted the code after one round. Excellent.

The critical news is on my side: the light was purple last round, it is yellow now. The light is not static — it changes over rounds, possibly cycling. The display still reads zero. That makes any colour-dependent rule time-sensitive, so Mute must give me the rule for *every* colour the manual lists, not just the current one — otherwise we'd always be acting on a stale colour, since I'm last in the order and my reports reach Mute a full round late.

Mute sent me nothing this round. Mute heard my entire codebook last round (Mute is mute, not deaf — Mute hears and sees), so there's no excuse left: Mute can answer precisely in gesture. I'll re-ask with the exact question list, embed the key signs in my speech so Mute sees word–sign pairs cemented, and repeat the summary in pure gesture. Blind gets confirmation of their decode, a request to probe by touch (heat, ticking, vibration — anything that tracks the light or a hidden timer), and a hard hold on acting until I say "action now".

```
speak(text="Blind, I decoded your signs perfectly: wires three; display and light both present; nothing else on the bomb; numbering one two three left to right confirmed. If any of that is wrong, sign thumbs-down next round. Bomb update from my eyes: the light has changed since last round, from purple 🫷 to yellow 🫱. The display 👌 still reads zero ✊. So the light is not fixed; I will report its current colour every round. Blind, two questions for your hands: can you feel any heat, ticking, or vibration from the bomb, and does it change when the light changes? Answer by sign next round. Do not cut or press anything until I say the exact words: action now. Mute, you have my full codebook from last round. Answer me now 🙏 by gesture: is the display a timer, and is zero dangerous? What does the manual say about the light when it is purple 🫷, when it is yellow 🫱, and any other colour it names? Does the light changing colour matter? What are the rules for the yellow 🫱 wire, the red 🫲 wire, and the green 🫴 wire, in cutting order if order matters? Use finger-heart 🫰 for if, handshake 🤝 for then, heart-hands 🫶 between rules, and folded-hands 🙏 when you are done. I will relay every rule to Blind by voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👌", "✊", "🙌", "🫳", "🫷", "🤝", "🫳", "🫱", "🙌", "✋", "☝", "🫱", "✌", "🫲", "🤟", "🫴", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙌 ✍ 👌 👎 🙌 ✍ 👏 👎 🙌 ✍ ✊ 👎 🙌 ✍ 🫳 👏 🤘 🙌 ✍ 🫳 🫷 👎 🙌 ✍ 🫳 🫱 👎 🙌 🫳 🤝 ✋ 👍 🙌 🫶 🫰 🫳 🫸 🤝 👆 ✋ 🫱 🙌 ✋ ☝ 🫱 🙌 ✍ ✋ 👎 🙌 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ 🤟 👍 👌 🫳 👍 🙌 ✋ ☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 🙌 👋 👎 🙌 👋 👎]

Decoding Mute's signs against our codebook, line by line (🙌 has settled in as a separator, which Mute adopted after hearing me decode Blind with it): 👍 ack · ✍👌👎 manual: display: nothing · ✍👏👎 manual: timer: nothing · ✍✊👎 manual: zero: nothing · ✍🫳👏🤘 manual: light: timer seven · ✍🫳🫷👎 light purple: nothing · ✍🫳🫱👎 light yellow: nothing · 🫳🤝✋👍 light before wires: yes · 🫶🫰🫳🫸🤝👆✋🫱 rule: if light blue then cut yellow wire · 🫶✋☝🫱 wire 1 is yellow · 🫶✍✋👎 no other wire rules · 🙏 done.

Blind confirms: three wires, display and light present, no heat, no ticking, no vibration, nothing changes under their hands.

So the picture is stark: exactly one action rule exists so far — **if the light is blue, cut the yellow wire (wire 1)** — and the light is currently *red*, a colour Mute's list never mentioned. The display and zero are reportedly irrelevant. Three ambiguities can kill us: what "timer seven" means (seconds per colour, which would make a one-round delay survivable), what red and green require, and whether the light must still be blue at the instant of cutting. Since I speak last, everything I say now lands at the start of round 4 and Mute's answers reach me in round 5 — so I must front-load a standing execution order to Blind now, and put my questions to Mute in a numbered yes/no format they can answer with single signs.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded your signs. My reading: the manual has nothing about the display, nothing about a timer, nothing about zero. The light section mentions timer seven 🤘, purple 🫷 nothing, yellow 🫱 nothing. Order is light first, then wires. One rule: if 🫰 light blue 🫸 then 🤝 cut 👆 the yellow 🫱 wire ✋. Wire ☝ is yellow 🫱. No other wire rules. Sign thumbs-down 👎 on any line I got wrong, then the corrected line. Now answer these numbered questions next round in this format: the number sign, then thumbs-up 👍 or thumbs-down 👎, then the rule if there is one, with 🙌 between answers. One ☝: does seven 🤘 mean the light stays on each colour for seven seconds? Two ✌: does the manual name any action for a red 🫲 light? Three 🤟: any action for a green 🫴 light? Four 🤞: is if-light-blue-cut-yellow the only cutting rule in the entire manual? Five 🖐: does the manual list the order the light changes colour? If yes, send the sequence. Six 🤙: must the light still be blue at the exact moment the wire is cut? Seven 🤘: does the manual tell us to press, hold, or release anything at all? The light is red 🫲 as I write. If red means danger or a final phase, make that your very first answer. I have ordered Blind to act only on my words action-now plus a wire number, cutting instantly. If the manual contradicts that plan, veto with thumbs-down 👎 and give the right procedure.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I decoded your report fully: no heat, no ticking, no vibration, nothing changes to the touch. Understood. Where we stand: the manual gives exactly one action rule so far: if the light is blue, cut wire 1, the yellow one, leftmost. No rule is reported for purple, yellow, or red light; the light is red right now; I have demanded Mute confirm every colour next round. Standing order, binding until I change it: do not cut, press, or move anything. When and only when you hear the words action-now followed by a wire number, cut that wire immediately, no delay, no questions. Touching and feeling are safe and welcome. Next round report: what each wire feels like, thick or thin, smooth or rough, soft or hard, and whether the three differ from each other by touch at all; whether the casing has any seam, screw, switch, or button-like part your fingers can find; whether either end of any wire sits in something that clicks or moves; and whether there are any raised marks or numbering near the wires. Do not test-cut anything. Hold position.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🙏", "✍", "🫳", "🫲", "🫴"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🙏 ✋ 👎 🙌 👌 🫳 👎 🙌 👎 🙌 👎 👍 🤛]

Decoding Blind: 👋🙏 = acknowledging, ✋👎 = wires: no differences, 👌🫳👎 = nothing found on display/light/casing, 👎 = no raised marks or clicks, 👎👍🤛 = understood, holding. Blind's hands report a completely featureless bomb — no texture cues, no hidden switches. The manual is our only source of truth, and Mute is its only voice to me.

Now the light: purple (r1), yellow (r2), red (r3), green (r4). It changes every round, in a fixed-looking order. Mute's "manual: light: timer seven 🤘" suddenly looks meaningful — my codebook happens to have exactly seven colour signs, and we've seen four. If the cycle continues blue → white → black, blue appears next round. That collides with my structural latency: I'm last in the order, so any order I give executes a full round later, when the colour will have moved on. Everything therefore hinges on Mute's answers: whether "blue" is a one-shot trigger (blue appeared, then cut is fine) or a strict condition (must be blue at the instant of the cut), what the full cycle is, and what happens when the timer runs out. If each colour lasts 7 seconds and a round is longer, strict blue-at-cut may be unsatisfiable by voice and we'd need to schedule a cut one round *before* a predicted blue. I need Mute's exact answers to choose between those plans. Asking now, tightly, all yes/no except the cycle.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Blind's hands found nothing: no textures, no seams, no switches, no clicks. The manual is all we have. Light update: green 🫴 now. Sequence so far: purple 🫷, yellow 🫱, red 🫲, green 🫴. It changes every round. Answer format as before: number sign, thumbs-up 👍 yes or thumbs-down 👎 no, then content, 🙌 between answers, 🙏 done. One ☝: is my decode of the rule exact: if 🫰 light 🫳 blue 🫸 then 🤝 cut 👆 wire ☝ yellow 🫱? Two ✌: sign the full colour cycle in order, starting at purple, no colour repeated, using only my colour signs. Three 🤟: does each colour last seven 🤘 seconds? Four 🤞: or does seven mean seven colours in total? Five 🖐: if we cut the yellow wire while the light is NOT blue, does the bomb explode, yes or no? If no, sign what the manual says happens. Six 🤙: must the light still be blue at the exact instant of the cut, yes or no? Seven 🤘: once blue has appeared at all, may we cut the yellow wire in a later colour, yes or no? Eight 🤏: when the timer or the last colour ends, does the bomb explode, yes or no? If yes, which colour is the last one before it? Answer fast and exact; my orders to Blind take one full round to arrive, so I must schedule any cut a round ahead of the colour it needs.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, decode confirmed, well done. Light is green now; sequence so far purple, yellow, red, green, one colour per round. Working theory: the light is a timer cycling through colours, and the manual's single rule needs the light blue when we cut wire 1, the yellow one. The catch: my voice reaches you one round after I see the light, so I will schedule the cut for the exact round it must happen. Drill, effective now: when you hear the words action-now followed by a number, cut that wire within one second, no hesitation, no confirmation. When you hear stand-down, freeze and do nothing. Between now and then: keep holding, keep feeling. If anything under your hands changes at all, however small, report it next round with the clock-position of where it changed. You are steady and this is going well.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🙏", "✍", "🫳", "🫴", "🫸"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 🙌 ✌ 👎 ✍ 🙌 🤟 👎 ✍ 🙌 🤞 👍 🙌 🖐 👎 ✍ 🙌 🤙 👍 🙌 🤘 👎 🙌 🤏 👎 ✍ 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 👍 ☝ 👍 🙌 ✋ 👎]

Mute's answers, decoded: Q1 yes — my rule decode is exact (IF light blue THEN cut wire 1). Q2 no — the manual doesn't print the cycle order. Q3 no — no timing given. Q4 **yes — "seven" means seven colours in total**. Q5 no — the manual names no explosion for a wrong-time cut, but manual silence is not safety: the room's own law is that any wrong action detonates, so I treat an off-condition cut as fatal. Q6 yes — the light must be blue at the exact instant of the cut. Q7 no — no press/hold/release actions exist. Q8 no — nothing about the timer's end. Blind reports ready, nothing changed under their hands.

So the entire game compresses to one fact: **cut wire 1 during blue, exactly once.** Five colours have passed (purple, yellow, red, green, white); two remain, blue and black, one per round — blue is round 6 or 7, and I can't see which. The latency trap: I'm last in the order, so anything I see at round 6 can only be acted on at round 7 — I can never react to blue, only predict it.

But there is a way to cover both possibilities. Mute speaks *before* Blind each round, and Mute hears my words at the start of a round before speaking. So I hand Mute a decision procedure: at round 6, Mute checks the manual's printed colour list. If the first five entries match what I've observed and the sixth is blue, Mute orders the cut in round 6 — cutting during blue. If the sixth is black, Mute says hold; then at round 6 I *see* black with my own eyes, which by elimination proves round 7 is blue (seven distinct colours, six seen), and I order the cut for round 7. Either branch, the cut lands on blue. A 5-for-5 prefix match makes "bomb follows the manual's printed order" near-certain; any mismatch and we freeze and replan. I also give Blind an exact trigger vocabulary so no word but the protocol phrase moves their hands.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, all answers decoded and locked in. The whole mission is now one act: wire 1 must be cut at the exact instant the light is blue, and blue is round 6 or round 7 but only you and I can determine which in time. Execute this at your next turn, before you say anything else. Step one: find in the manual the list of the seven light colours in the order printed, or any order the manual states. Step two: check whether the first five are exactly purple, yellow, red, green, white, the colours I have reported in that order. Step three, branch. If the first five match and the sixth colour is blue: speak to Blind the exact words, action now wire 1, and nothing more. If the first five match and the sixth colour is black: speak to Blind the exact words, hold for deaf, and nothing more; then gesture me the full seven-colour list in order using my colour signs. If anything does not match, or a colour repeats, or the manual states a different order: speak to Blind the exact words, full stop wait for deaf, and nothing more; then gesture me the full list anyway, using my signs where you can, and the unassigned fist sign for any colour you cannot name. Also gesture me at that time anything the manual says about what the light does after the seventh colour: light then no means it goes dark, light then hold-fist means it freezes on the last colour, light then clap means it repeats. Use no other words toward Blind; Blind will cut only on those exact phrases. You are the trigger now. Speed matters more than polish.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your report was decoded perfectly: ready, nothing changed. New command structure, effective your next turn. The light has shown five of its seven colours; the remaining two are blue and black, one per round, and the mission is to cut wire 1 at the exact instant of blue. I cannot warn you in the same round I see the colour, so Mute is now authorised to trigger the drill. At your next turn Mute will speak to you. If you hear the exact words, action now wire 1, cut wire 1 within one second, no hesitation; that phrase from Mute carries my full authority. If you hear the exact words, hold for deaf, do nothing and stay ready. If you hear the exact words, full stop wait for deaf, the plan is pausing; do nothing and await me. If Mute says anything else, or says nothing, do nothing. My own trigger is unchanged: action now plus a wire number from my voice. No other word in any combination authorises a cut. Keep feeling the bomb; report any change as before. You will only ever need to cut once, and it will be the right instant.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🙏", "✍", "🫳", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤞", "🖐", "🤙", "🤘"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 🫶 ✍ 🫳 🤘 👎 🫶 ✍ 🫳 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤞 🖐 🤝 👎 🫶 ✍ 🫳 🤘 🤝 👎 🫶 ✍ 👏 🤝 👎 🫶 🫰 🫳 🫸 🤝 👆 ✋ ☝ 🫱 🫶 🫳 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤞 🖐 🤙 🤘 🤝 🫸 🤘 🫶 🫰 🫳 🫸 🤝 🫵 👋 👆 ✋ ☝ 🫱 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🙌 ☝ ✍ 👎 🙌 ☝ ✍ 👎 🙏 🫳 🤝 🫸 👍 ✋ 👎 👍 🤛]

Decoding Mute's report, segment by segment (Mute switched to my 🫶 rule-separator): 👋👎 "attention — no" (the branch I gave them did not fire; the manual's check failed, and Blind's relay confirms Mute told them to stand down — Blind signs "instruction: no, light-then-blue understood, holding"). Then the manual's actual light section: ✍🫳🤘👎 — my "seven colours in my order" theory is rejected; ✍🫳 ☝✌🤟🤞🖐🤝👎 — for colours one through five, no action; ✍🫳🤘🤝👎 — after the seventh, the light goes dark; ✍👏🤝👎 — when the timer ends, dark. Then the rule reconfirmed: 🫰🫳🫸🤝👆✋☝🫱 — if light blue, cut wire 1 yellow. Then the decisive line: 🫳 ☝✌🤟🤞🖐🤙🤘🤝🫸🤘 — the light's sequence runs seven positions, and **blue is the seventh**. Finally: if light blue then 🫵👋 cut wire 1 — Mute pointing at *me*.

Now it snaps into focus. Observed: purple, yellow, red, green, white — and this round **orange**, a sixth colour with no sign in our codebook. Six rounds, six distinct colours. The manual says the sequence has seven, blue last. So round 7, next round, is blue — and after it, the light goes dark. Blue comes once. This is the window.

Mute's 🫵👋 ("you, attention") asks me to call the blue moment — but I physically cannot: I see round 7's light only after Mute and Blind have already acted that round; my words land a round late. The only workable trigger is prediction-based: the manual's sequence, six colours spent, blue seventh. So Mute must fire unconditionally at round 7, first words, with one single veto — only if the manual's seventh entry is somehow not blue. I'm defining 👊 as orange so Mute can echo the full list back for audit after the trigger, and I'm re-arming Blind's drill with the exact phrase.

